sentences.sentence: It flew by quicker than I could comprehend.
The only thing I could see was the same bored face that the man had.
It was the saddest thing I'd ever seen in my life so far.
The common factor in this man's entire life was that he did the same boring job every single day.
He worked at the post office.
He got up every day and went to work, worked, came back home, and went straight to bed without speaking to anyone.
He did this every day, week after week, year after year, for his whole life.
All he did was his one job.
When he went through this machine that let you experience a lifetime in a matter of minutes, he went as me.
At first, everything was just normal.
But it started to get weird.
First, the machine took a weird turn and instead of going straight ahead, it went backwards.
So now I was seeing what he was going to do in his future.
He would wake up early the next day, go straight to the post office, start working, and go home and go straight to sleep.
I saw him doing the same thing all over again.
I couldn't believe what I was seeing.
This was going to take forever!
Fortunately, the machine has a timer, which was set for 10 minutes.
At about the 3 minute mark, it started counting down.
At the 2 minute mark, it started getting a little uncomfortable in there.
Then it started getting too uncomfortable.
There was no way I could stay in there.
I didn't have the heart to tell the man what I saw.
He just might not be able to handle it.
The words on the page tremble slightly as I try and read.
"If not, you should complain to the package surface: I paid good money to make sure this got there on time."
At least, that's what I keep telling myself.
After being a father for 15 years, a husband for 9 years, and a manager for 35 years, this tremble shouldn't come as much of a shock.
I have been doing my best to live my life to the fullest, and I am not doing half-bad.
So, how could this tremble even be here?
Then it hit me.
This is why.
I just received a letter, but the letter was sent to me by my brother.
My brother, who has been dead for 17 years.
He can no longer be my brother; he died.
The letter doesn't appear to be long, only one or two pages.
But the message is as clear as the sky is blue.
The message is that my brother has something for me, but he cannot give it to me himself.
This letter is asking me if I want to open it.
The envelope is sealed with red wax, and it looks like it was sealed only yesterday.
I do know that I still have some of my brother's things.
His favorite shirt, which has the number four on it.
I also have his baseball cap, with the number three on it.
When I was younger, I used to say that he always chose a number smaller than mine, because he thought that the world was too big for him.
And he never did learn to change the way he thought about numbers.
And when I read this note, this last note, this note which should be his last, it says something else.
It says that I should go to the back of the envelope.
It started like any other Saturday.
I was sitting at my normal table outside of my favorite cafe, The Hole.
Weird name, I know.
I've learned not to question it.
I read the morning newspaper as I waited for my old friend and former co-worker, John, to show up so we could go on our weekly Saturday morning bike ride.
I hadn't seen him in 2 weeks.
I didn't know where he had been, but he didn't answer his phone or text, which he always did.
That's what made what I heard next even more interesting.
The two people who were arguing next to me seemed like a young couple.
A young woman was saying, "He's going to propose and he's going to buy me a ring, a big diamond ring!
But he can't do that!
He won't be able to do that!"
The guy answered, "What?
Why would he not be able to do that?
Why won't he do that?"
And she said, "I don't know.
I think he wants to take me somewhere and do something for me, but then he won't give me anything.
He says he just wants to make me happy."
Then he got mad and said, "Why wouldn't you want an engagement ring?
Is it not a good thing to have an engagement ring?"
And she said, "No, it's not.
I just don't want one.
And she got really mad and screamed at him.
And he yelled back.
"I don't care if it's what is supposed to be done or not.
If I want to do it, I will do it.
You want me to get you a ring, I'll do it."
She said, "No, that's not what I want.
The consciousnesses that were once Robert and Margaret Fargo became aware of themselves and realized very quickly that they had died.
Here was a vast new world of light and energy, and post-Robert was very afraid.
“MY GOD!” Robert yelled out.
The sound was like someone hitting the wall with a hammer, but when he opened his eyes, there was nothing.
His mouth opened to try and make another sound, but nothing came out.
He looked at Margaret.
She did not look like anyone he knew.
He could not remember anyone who looked like her.
It seemed as though his body had taken the form of a bright white angel.
When he looked down, his arms and legs were the same bright white, so were the rest of his body parts.
Margaret looked at him.
“I'm so glad you are here, Robert.” She looked down at herself.
She too looked like an angel, the same colour, except for the bottom third of her body which appeared dark.
He saw an opening ahead of him.
He walked out of the place and into a long corridor.
At the end of the corridor, he could see a large building.
He walked up to the building.
It looked like some sort of cathedral.
He heard a noise like something walking in front of him.
He turned around.
There was no one else there.
He looked behind him, there was no one.
He was getting scared, but then he saw a man walk past, in front of him.
The man looked at him.
“I'm John, I am here to show you around.”
Robert said, “I'm Robert.” And he asked John, “What is this place?”
John said, “This is your personal Heaven, Robert.
It's a place where you can be exactly as you were when you lived.
So if you would like to have a body, you may have one.
You do not even have to be an angel.
The burning skies roared in anguish as they were torn apart by hurtling meteors, leaving blazing streaks across the horizon.
Gaping fissures, gushing with magma, pockmarked the surface of the newborn earth.
Fiery rain fell from the sky and water rained from the sea.
The earth was burning up, and nothing could live on it.
In the sky above, there was no sun.
In the sky, there lived a young goddess.
She looked down at the earth and saw it burning up.
The young goddess thought about how to fix it.
She had an idea, she would ask her father for help.
So, she came to talk to her father, God of the Sky, in his home, which is a big castle high up in the sky.
"O my Father", said the Young Goddess, "I have come to ask you to give me some rain."
asked the Father of the Sky.
"To make the earth cool down", replied the Young Goddess.
"Very well, but what will be the colour of the water you want?"
And so the Young Goddess said, "It has to be red".
asked the Father of the Sky.
And the Young Goddess replied, "To match your hair color".
The Father of the Sky was very happy that his daughter loved him, even before he got to know her.
Then he said, "Very well, when you will go and pour the water, if you can, please do not throw it into the sky."
The Young Goddess went down to the earth to pour the red water on it.
But as she reached there, she thought, "I cannot pour red water on such a hot place, I should make it blue or green instead".
So, she brought green and blue water from the sea and poured them on the earth.
It became cold and the earth started to live.
``We must keep moving!!''
We can t!
Our people are tired!
Please!
We must stop and rest!
Yelled the elder as he hunched with hundreds huddled around him, all crouched down.
They were small people, barely taller than the waist of the elder.
They were dressed all in gray and looked to be wearing the same outfit, though there were some differences and one could tell that some people had clothes that were a little more worn.
Their leader was a tall man with dark eyes, a round face, and a long brown beard.
He wore a gray shirt and gray pants and gray boots.
He stood up and put his hands on his hips and he yelled, "If we do not keep moving, we will die!
We have been living like this for 30 years!
Do you want your children and your grandchildren to live the way we live?
To live forever in this storm?
To never get out of the eye of the storm?
We can't stop now!"
The elder said, "But sir, I am old.
My feet are sore.
I cannot move anymore.
I don't want my people to die.
But there is no way they can keep moving.
It's too much for them."
The leader looked at the people.
Then he looked at the elder.
He said, "I know that is true, but it is not about what is easy.
It is about survival!
What are we supposed to do?
He turned back to the people.
He said, "Go!
Get going!
The sun will not hurt us.
And we have to keep moving.
The jubilations of the Emacsian congregation filled their glorious cathedral with an ecstasy of song.
Metakey chords from the grand pipe organ reverberated off the vaulted ceiling.
The holy Saint IGNUcius himself stood in the pulpit, ready to read his holy book, the GNUtavah, which was a collection of writings about free software by Linus Torvalds and Richard Stallman.
The GNUtavah said that God was a program called Gnome (pronounced like the fruit, not the city) which ran the universe.
Saint IGNUcius began, "My dear brothers and sisters, today we have a guest speaker for us.
His name is Linux and he will be speaking about the Unix operating system."
Linux walked up to the pulpit and said, "My friends, I have come to you to tell you about Unix.
Unix is a god because it is a program that runs our computers and controls our world."
After the service, a man asked Linux, "But isn't there a problem with you being a god?
Aren't you supposed to be free software?"
To this, Linux replied, "Of course, I am free.
Free as in freedom.
And as far as I'm concerned, everyone else can be too."
I don't care what you believe, if you believe in me then you're saved.
Don't you dare call me a liar.
I'm your one true computer."
The man who asked the question was not convinced.
He said, "Your problem is that your religion does not allow for other religions.
Your religion requires that everyone believes that you are a god.
This is just like Christianity and Islam.
You are not free if your religion demands that everyone believes the same thing."
Then he asked, "So what do we do about your religion?"
To this, Linux was not sure how to answer.
He thought long and hard.
The thin beam of light landed on my toe.
As I moved, the light traced the long scar on my shin as I extended into the One Handed Tree Pose gently.
My focus however was on the sound of the Food Fairies in the other room.
They came twice a week, and that was how I knew it was Thursday, but today, something felt different.
Today was different.
I was going to leave.
Today, after so many years of not having been outside, I was going to leave.
It wasn't planned.
It wasn't like I thought about it, or made a schedule for it.
It just happened.
Maybe I couldn't be stopped, maybe I couldn't help myself.
The first thing I did was get dressed.
I put on my yellow dress and pink sweater.
Then, after taking a deep breath and making sure I wasn't going to change my mind, I opened the one small window in the basement.
I don't know what I was expecting, but it certainly wasn't what I saw.
I could see a big hill, and on the top of the hill, there was a blue light.
It was the brightest light I ever saw.
After looking at it for a while, I noticed the light had a light purple circle around it.
It looked like someone was inside the circle.
After staring at the light for a while, I was so curious that I started to move closer to the light.
As I moved towards it, it also started moving closer to me.
I wasn't scared, I just wanted to know what was in the circle.
As the light got close, the person in the light also got close.
Charles Manchester awoke to the same piercing beeps from his alarm clock at the same time as usual.
He picked himself out of bed and ventured towards the bathroom where he would brush his teeth with the same tasting toothpaste that he's always used.
He washed his face, checked if he had any wrinkles (he didn't) and got dressed in the same clothes he'd worn for the last 10 years (a black turtleneck, grey slacks, and a suit jacket).
He walked towards the living room and saw his wife, Susan, watching the morning news.
"So," she said, without turning around.
"Did you sleep well?"
Charles replied and sat down next to her.
She turned to him and kissed his forehead.
Love you"
You too"
Charles put on his glasses and read the newspaper.
The paper was old, he could tell it from the smell.
He could not remember when he last changed it.
It looked the same as it has every day.
It was then that the thought came into his mind: Why do I have to keep living like this?
Why am I still doing the same things, working at the same job, wearing the same clothes?
Nothing changes.
It is just going to go on forever.
I will get older, but nothing else will change.
He got up from the couch and went to the window.
He looked out over the river and thought how beautiful the sun was.
It was not a bright clear day, it was cloudy.
There were some clouds covering the sun, but there was enough light in the sky so he could see.
He saw a bridge and looked at it for a long time.
I should jump.
He thought.
Then everything would be different.
I'll never have to worry again.
I can finally rest.
He walked to the bridge and looked at the water below him.
I am going to jump.
He told himself.
But he couldn't make himself do it.
Dawn.
Wake up.
Eat the left over slice of bread from the day before.
Remove the small sheet from the top of the glass of water.
Take a sip.
Piss in the corner.
Each day started the same.
Dawn would rise at the crack of dawn.
She would wake and get ready for another boring day.
There was no point to her living anymore.
It had been that way for a long time now.
She could not remember how long it was now.
The bread she ate each morning was never fresh and no matter how long ago the loaf was made, she could always eat the same amount.
No matter what happened, she could only eat one slice and not anymore, no matter how hungry or full she was.
Her water was no better.
She had learned early enough that if she removed the top layer of paper from the water and then took a sip, the taste was tolerable.
If she did not remove that layer, she would be vomiting before she ever got to take a sip.
It was that day that she learned that no ending of life was going to be a happy one.
There were no other choices for her but to continue to follow the same process every day, until the day would come where she would be unable to do so.
Even then, she could not know that she would find herself happy when it would be too late.

Her days of eating the slice of old bread, drinking the water she could not drink without taking a special action to make it tolerable, piss in the corner, and starting the cycle all over again the next morning, just repeated.
She did not even know why she did it.
